items.stem:
In a practical class in Lucknow, students ground a piece of liver in trichloroacetic acid and filtered it through cheesecloth.
(i) What are the filtrate and the retentate called? (1 mark)
(ii) Name two classes of compounds in the retentate. (1 mark)
(iii) Why do lipids appear in the retentate though their molecular weight is low? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Filtrate – acid-soluble pool; retentate – acid-insoluble fraction. (ii) Proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides (and lipids). (iii) On grinding, cell membranes and other membranes break into pieces that form water-insoluble vesicles, which separate with the acid-insoluble fraction.

items.stem: Which term describes organic compounds with identifiable functions in normal physiological processes, such as amino acids, sugars and nucleotides?
items.answer: primary metabolites

primary metabolites

items.stem: Describe the four levels of protein structure. Give examples of proteins and their functions.
items.answer: Primary – sequence of amino acids, N-terminal to C-terminal; secondary – folding of the chain into helix (right-handed) or sheet; tertiary – 3-D folding of the helical chain like a hollow woollen ball, necessary for biological activity; quaternary – assembly of more than one polypeptide/subunit, e.g. haemoglobin (2α + 2β). Examples: collagen – intercellular ground substance; trypsin – enzyme; insulin – hormone; antibody – fights infections; receptor – sensory reception; GLUT-4 – glucose transport.
items.markingKey: 3 marks levels; 2 marks examples.

items.stem: Describe the factors affecting enzyme activity. Explain with a graph the effect of substrate concentration.
items.answer: Temperature and pH – each enzyme has an optimum; activity declines above and below; high temperature denatures. Substrate concentration – velocity rises and then reaches Vmax as active sites are saturated; Km. Inhibitors – competitive inhibitors resemble the substrate (malonate for succinic dehydrogenase). items.stem: Explain the catalytic cycle of an enzyme action in steps.
items.answer: Substrate binds to the active site; the enzyme alters its shape to fit more tightly (ES complex); chemical bonds of the substrate are broken and new enzyme–product complex forms; the enzyme releases the products and is free to bind another substrate.
items.markingKey: ¾ mark each step.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a metal ion and a coenzyme on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A non-protein part of an enzyme has these features: e.g. NAD and NADP contain niacin. Identify the type of cofactor – a metal ion or a coenzyme? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) A metal ion: forms coordination bonds with side chains at the active site; also forms coordination bonds with the substrate; e.g. zinc for carboxypeptidase. A coenzyme: organic compound; association with the apoenzyme is transient, during catalysis; many contain vitamins. (b) A coenzyme.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: a coenzyme; 1 mark: “e.g. NAD and NADP contain niacin” is a feature of a coenzyme.

items.stem: What is meant by “activation energy”?
items.answer: The energy needed to convert the substrate into the transition state.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the energy needed to convert the substrate into the transition state.

items.stem: Give three differences between nucleic acids and polysaccharides.
items.answer: Nucleic acids: polynucleotides; monomers joined by phosphodiester bonds; contain a pentose sugar and nitrogenous bases. Polysaccharides: e.g. cellulose, starch, glycogen; monomers joined by glycosidic bonds; starch stores energy in plants.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. nucleic acids – polynucleotides; monomers joined by phosphodiester bonds; contain a pentose sugar and nitrogenous bases; polysaccharides – e.g. cellulose, starch, glycogen; monomers joined by glycosidic bonds; starch stores energy in plants.

items.stem: A double-stranded DNA sample has 20% adenine. What is the percentage of guanine in it?
items.markingKey: (a) By Chargaff's rule A = T and G = C; adenine = thymine = 20%, so the other two bases are each (100 − 40)/2 = 30%. Hence guanine = 30%.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between polysaccharides and lipids on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A biomolecule has these features: monomers joined by glycosidic bonds. Identify the class of biomolecule – polysaccharides or lipids? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Polysaccharides: long chains of sugars; monomers joined by glycosidic bonds; e.g. cellulose, starch, glycogen. Lipids: generally water insoluble; may be simple fatty acids or glycerides; phospholipids are found in cell membranes. (b) Polysaccharides.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: polysaccharides; 1 mark: “monomers joined by glycosidic bonds” is a feature of polysaccharides.
